faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer:
## Welcome Evening
Garden casual — sundresses, linen shirts, light layers for the evening breeze. No jackets required.

## Ceremony & Reception
Garden formal: midi or floor-length dresses, suits or a blazer with trousers. Ties optional, seasonal colors encouraged.

note: The ceremony and cocktail hour are on grass — block heels and wedges will be much happier than stilettos.

faq.question: Is the wedding indoors or outdoors?
faq.answer:
A little of both — and all on one property.

- Ceremony: outdoors in the rose garden
- Cocktail hour: outdoors on the citrus lawn
- Dinner & dancing: inside the glasshouse

Santa Barbara evenings cool off fast once the sun drops, so bring a light layer for after dark.

faq.question: How do we get to the estate? Is there parking?
faq.answer:
The easiest way is the shuttle — it leaves from The Aveline Hotel at 3:00 PM and brings everyone back at the end of the night.

If you’d rather drive, there is on-site parking at the estate, and cars may be left overnight and collected by noon Sunday.

note: Shuttle route: The Aveline Hotel → Rosehill Garden Estate → The Aveline Hotel. Return departures at 11:00 PM and 11:45 PM.

faq.question: Can I bring a plus-one?
faq.answer: Plus-ones are by invitation only — if your invitation includes a guest, their name (or “and guest”) appears on the envelope. We wish we could host everyone, but the glasshouse only holds so many.

faq.question: Are kids invited?
faq.answer: We love your little ones, but apart from the children in our own families this is an adults-only celebration. Consider it a night off — the dance floor will thank you.

faq.question: When should we RSVP by?
faq.answer:
Please reply by May 1, 2027. Our caterer needs final counts well ahead of the weekend, so we sadly can’t accommodate responses after that date.

If your plans change after you reply, just call Ana at (805) 555-0134.

story.paragraph: We met in the spring of 2021, in the back row of a Tuesday-night pottery class neither of us had planned to attend alone. Ana was there because her sister gifted her the course; Ben was there because his roommate bailed at the last minute. Her first bowl collapsed on the wheel. His exploded in the kiln. We have been laughing at the same disasters ever since.

Our first real date was a farmers-market breakfast that turned into an all-day drive up the coast — windows down, one shared playlist, no plan past lunch. Somewhere past Gaviota we realized we had been talking for nine hours straight. Two years, one small apartment, and one very opinionated cat later, that coast drive had become our anniversary tradition.

story.heading: The proposal
story.paragraph: Last October, Ben suggested a sunset walk through the rose garden by the old mission — the same garden we had wandered on our third date. He had recruited Ana’s best friend to hide behind a hedge with a camera, forgot every word of the speech he had practiced for weeks, and managed only the one question that mattered. She said yes before he finished asking.

Now we’re getting married under the oaks at Rosehill, ten minutes from where it all clicked into place, with the people we love most in the world. Thank you for being part of our story — we can’t wait to see you in June.
